metadata:

**Why:** adults are linear on 1-100. The novelty margin is thin, since it only passes the 0.002 threshold because of the prior pull.
**How to apply:** don't retry magnitude-compression variants. See [[grid-tabulated-range-evidence]], [[number-game-refinement-findings]].

---
name: normative-distortions-collapse
description: exp2 iter_3 c2: exponent distortions of the normative concept learner all collapse; target-only final-digit binding error eps≈0.04 survives
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested in exp2 iter_3/candidate_2 (2026-11-01) as MAP screens on the uniform-stray, family-only, Beta-reliability learner (MAP ll -2031.2). Each one collapsed to the normative value:
- set log-lik × n^-gamma: gamma 0.04
- size exponent beta: 0.94
- interval width prior rho: -0.08
- range-only size exponent: 0.96 (+0.6 ll)
- Gaussian target noise for range membership: sigma≈0.5
- final-digit binding error applied to the examples: eps→0

What was submitted: final_digit_binding_errors. Under "ends in d", only the target check accepts a number with d in the tens place, at rate eps. MAP eps is 0.037 (+0.1 ll), with posterior 90% CI [.008, .08]. Its p_yes differs from the normative fit by RMSE 0.009 on the data trials. It runs at 3.3 ms/grad with about 27 steps at 0.99.
Speed trick: with uniform strays, rules and intervals both use one (n,k,size) table. Cells read their set's posterior through a one-hot (cells,sets) pt.dot, and interval sums are pt.dot(counts, lik.T) masked by a one-hot on n. This was 3x faster than gathers.
**How to apply:** don't spend normative+distortion slots on exponents. Cell-level residuals (e.g. 16,26,96→67 at 5/5) are a better place to look. See [[noisy-criterion-decision-rule]], [[fast-incumbent-sampling]].
---
name: number-game-refinement-findings
description: Which refinements of the number-game Bayesian concept incumbent help or are dead ends (iter_2, 2026-10-30)
metadata:
  type: project
---
Tested in iter_2/candidate_4 (2026-10-30) against inferred_example_noise_concepts (MAP loglik -817.3, my per-row LOO -842.3..-842.9, p_loo ~22):
- Offset arithmetic progressions (c mod k) as an extra rule group: +0.4 MAP loglik only, so a near-duplicate.
- Bounded rules (rule ∩ interval): the share went to 0, so a duplicate.
- Family-only rule weights (7 families, equal within): MAP 16 nats worse.
- Hierarchical (partially pooled, non-centred) rule weights around family levels: LOO -841.8 (+0.6..1.2), p_loo 14, distinct predictions (RMSE 0.022). Submitted as family_pooled_rule_prior.
Data facts: 5 participants, each did the same 450-trial sequence (blocks of 450 rows), with no individual differences in yes-rate. Calibration by set size is already good and the residuals look like noise.
**Why:** the incumbent is near ceiling, so gains come from cutting effective parameters, not from new concepts.
**How to apply:** future refinements should target prior structure or parsimony; skip hypothesis-space additions. See [[interval-tempering-speed-trick]].
---
name: fuzzy-and-centre-weighted-ranges
description: exp2 iter_3: any non-uniform within-range generator or graded range readout loses; uniform sharp intervals optimal; subset pre-sum speed trick
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp2 iter_3 cand_0 (2026-11-01). Base: familiar_strays_family_level_prior (MAP ll −2031 in my prof script). Swapped in variants of the interval part:
- Gaussian clusters (log-σ grid, integer μ, typicality readout): −2093. Box readout at 1.5σ: −2084. Generalised-normal β 4–16: −2079 (the grid and log-σ prior cost ~45 nats).
- One cluster per interval (μ = midpoint, σ = w/√12), uniform prior. Fuzzy generation + typicality readout: −2114. Gaussian generation + sharp membership: −2047. Uniform generation + typicality readout: −2098.
- Truncated within-range generation, σ = w/√12, w/4, w/2: −2047, −2058, −2033. Edge-weighted (1/kernel), σ = w/√12 and w/2: −2047, −2033. Uniform is the optimum in both directions.
Submitted centre_weighted_range_sampling (σ = w/√12, −2047 MAP, smoke OK).
**Why:** the data want sharp, uniform ranges. Graded readouts are the worst part.
**How to apply:** don't propose fuzzy or typicality-graded magnitude concepts again. Speed trick: for any parameter-free per-example generator g_h, pre-sum Π_{i∈J} g_h(x_i) over h per subset J (16 per set, plus target-weighted per cell). Evidence = Σ_J c_|J| W_J G_J. That gives 2.9 ms/grad over all 5050 ranges, against 240 ms for the explicit (sets, H, 4) form.
Related: [[compressed-number-line-ranges]], [[grid-tabulated-range-evidence]], [[graded-exemplar-uncertain-reliability]]

"""Familiar strays with rules that people may confine to the examples' magnitude stretch.

Refinement of rule_count_familiar_strays. People do the same Bayesian concept
learning over 45 equally plausible rules and every interval of 1-100, with the
size principle, an uncertain (Beta-marginalised) belief about the program's
reliability, and strays that are uniform or "familiar" (familiarity = how many
rules contain the number). The one change is the concept space: people also
consider a rule confined to a stretch of the number line, i.e. a contiguous
run of a rule's consecutive members (e.g. "even numbers from 52 to 88",
"multiples of 7 from 14 to 42"), excluding the full rule. These restricted
rules take an inferred share rho of the rule prior lambda_0, split equally over
rules and then equally over each rule's runs. Because a short run is small, the
size principle favours it when the examples fit a rule and cluster, so people
endorse rule members inside the examples' range more than members far outside.

Concept evidence uses the same exact reliability marginal as the incumbent:
p(X | h) is proportional to sum_j s^-j e_j(h) B(u + j, v + n - j) / B(u, v),
with e_j(h) the elementary symmetric polynomials of 1 / q(x_i) over the
examples h contains. A restricted rule enters only through (the subset of
examples it contains, its size), so prepare_observed tabulates prior mass by
(subset, size) per set and per (set, target).

import numpy as np

        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),

    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules

"""Graded exemplar retrieval of stored number concepts, with familiar strays
and an equal prior over rules.

Refinement of graded_exemplar_familiar_strays. People hold number concepts as
stored member lists (45 rules and every magnitude range of 1-100) and compare
numbers by number-line similarity s = r^|x - y|. A concept is retrieved in
proportion to its prior times, per example, a mixture of the example's mean
similarity to its members and a stray (uniform, or with inferred probability
mix a "familiar" number: a random member of a random rule), with an uncertain
reliability a ~ Beta integrated out per set; a target is endorsed by its
similarity to the nearest stored member of each retrieved concept.
The one change (taken from familiar_strays_equal_rule_prior): people have no
preference among kinds of rule, so all 45 rules share the rules' prior share
lambda_0 equally, and which rule is retrieved is decided only by how well and
how tightly its members resemble the examples.

E_a prod_i (a s_i + (1 - a) q_i) = prod_i q_i * sum_S c_|S| prod_{i in S} s_i / q_i;
range evidence is tabulated per set/subset on a logit(r) grid in prepare_observed.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
MAX_N = 4
GRID = np.linspace(-8.0, -1.5, 88)  # logit(r): r up to 0.18
MAX_D = 14  # r^15 < 1e-11 on this grid, so farther members add nothing
GRID_STEP = GRID[1] - GRID[0]


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


_RULES = rule_concepts()
RULE_NAMES, RULES = list(_RULES), list(_RULES.values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")
RULE_SIZE = RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1)
ABS_DIFF = np.abs(NUMBERS[:, None] - NUMBERS[None, :]).astype("float64")
RULE_DMIN = np.array([np.where(m[None, :] > 0, ABS_DIFF, np.inf).min(axis=1) for m in RULE_MEMBERSHIP])

STRAY_RULE_GEN = (RULE_MEMBERSHIP / RULE_SIZE[:, None]).mean(axis=0)  # (100,)
SUBSETS = np.array([[(m >> i) & 1 for i in range(MAX_N)] for m in range(2**MAX_N)], dtype=bool)  # (16, 4)
SUBSET_SIZE = SUBSETS.sum(axis=1)

_N = np.arange(1, MAX_N + 1, dtype="float64")[:, None]
_J = np.arange(MAX_N + 1, dtype="float64")[None, :]
_VALID = _J <= _N
_N_MINUS_J = np.maximum(_N - _J, 0.0)


def _betaln(a, b):
    return pt.gammaln(a) + pt.gammaln(b) - pt.gammaln(a + b)


def _elementary(weights, lib=pt):
    """Elementary symmetric polynomials e_0..e_4 over the last axis (4 examples)."""
    ones = lib.ones_like(weights[..., 0])
    e = [ones] + [ones * 0.0] * MAX_N
    for i in range(MAX_N):
        w = weights[..., i]
        e = [e[0]] + [e[j] + w * e[j - 1] for j in range(1, MAX_N + 1)]
    return lib.stack(e, axis=-1)


def range_tables(example_idx, example_mask, cell_set, cell_target):
    """Per logit(r) grid point: log sum over ranges of prod_{i in S} 100 s_i(h)
    per set and subset S, and the same weighted by each cell target's
    similarity to the range (cells, S)."""
    lo = np.array([m for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)], dtype="float64")[:, None]
    hi = np.array([n for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)], dtype="float64")[:, None]
    size = hi - lo + 1
    x = NUMBERS[None, :].astype("float64")
    inside = (x >= lo) & (x <= hi)
    dmin = np.maximum(0.0, np.maximum(lo - x, x - hi))
    S, C = example_idx.shape[0], len(cell_set)
    K = len(SUBSETS)
    log_set = np.zeros((len(GRID), S, K))
    log_cell = np.zeros((len(GRID), C, K))
    cells_of = [np.where(cell_set == s)[0] for s in range(S)]
    for g, logit_r in enumerate(GRID):
        r = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-logit_r))
        geo = r / (1 - r)
        summed = np.where(
            inside,
            1 + geo * (2 - r ** np.where(inside, x - lo, 0) - r ** np.where(inside, hi - x, 0)),
            r**dmin * (1 - r**size) / (1 - r),
        )
        w100 = 100.0 * summed / size  # (ranges, numbers)
        endorse = r**dmin  # (ranges, numbers)
        for s in range(S):
            wts = w100[:, example_idx[s]] * example_mask[s][None, :]  # (ranges, 4)
            prods = np.prod(np.where(SUBSETS[None, :, :], wts[:, None, :], 1.0), axis=2)  # (ranges, 16)
            log_set[g, s] = np.log(np.maximum(prods.sum(axis=0), 1e-300))
            cs = cells_of[s]
            if len(cs):
                num = endorse[:, cell_target[cs]].T @ prods  # (k, 16)
                log_cell[g, cs] = np.log(np.maximum(num, 1e-300))
    return log_set, log_cell


with pm.Model() as model:
    example_idx = pm.Data("example_idx", np.zeros((1, MAX_N), dtype="int64"))  # x - 1
    example_mask = pm.Data("example_mask", np.zeros((1, MAX_N)))
    set_n_idx = pm.Data("set_n_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    range_log_e = pm.Data("range_log_e", np.zeros((len(GRID), 1, len(SUBSETS))))  # (grid, sets, S)
    range_log_cell = pm.Data("range_log_cell", np.zeros((len(GRID), 1, len(SUBSETS))))  # (grid, cells, S)
    cell_set = pm.Data("cell_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cell_target = pm.Data("cell_target", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # target - 1
    cell_n_idx = pm.Data("cell_n_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # (cells,): n - 1
    ex_rule_dcount = pm.Data("ex_rule_dcount", np.zeros((1, MAX_N, N_RULES, MAX_D + 1)))  # members at distance d
    cell_flat = pm.Data("cell_flat", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set * 100 + target - 1
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    alpha_logit = pm.Normal("alpha_logit", mu=2.2, sigma=1.5)
    alpha = pm.Deterministic("alpha", pm.math.sigmoid(alpha_logit))
    log_kappa = pm.Normal("log_kappa", mu=np.log(10.0), sigma=1.0)
    kappa = pm.Deterministic("kappa", pt.exp(log_kappa))
    u, v = alpha * kappa, (1 - alpha) * kappa

    # Number-line similarity gradient s(x, y) = r^|x - y|.
    r_logit = pm.TruncatedNormal("r_logit", mu=-4.0, sigma=1.0, lower=GRID[0], upper=GRID[-1])
    r = pm.Deterministic("r", pm.math.sigmoid(r_logit))
    log_r = pt.log(r)

    c_table = pt.where(_VALID, pt.exp(_betaln(u + _J, v + _N_MINUS_J) - _betaln(u, v)), 0.0)
    c_set = c_table[set_n_idx]  # (sets, j)

    # Stray distribution: uniform mixed with a random member of a random rule.
    mix_logit = pm.Normal("mix_logit", mu=0.0, sigma=1.5)
    mix = pm.Deterministic("mix", pm.math.sigmoid(mix_logit))
    rho = 1.0 / ((1 - mix) + mix * 100.0 * STRAY_RULE_GEN)  # (numbers,): 1 / (100 q)
    rho_ex = rho[example_idx]  # (sets, 4); masked examples have zero weight anyway
    rho_sub = pt.prod(pt.where(SUBSETS[None, :, :], rho_ex[:, None, :], 1.0), axis=2)  # (sets, 16)
    w_sub = c_set[:, SUBSET_SIZE] * rho_sub  # (sets, 16)

    # Rules: mean similarity of each example to the rule's stored members.
    r_pow = pt.exp(log_r * np.arange(MAX_D + 1))
    w_rule = 100.0 * pt.dot(ex_rule_dcount, r_pow) / RULE_SIZE  # (sets, 4, rules), masked via counts
    e_rule = _elementary((w_rule * rho_ex[:, :, None]).dimshuffle(0, 2, 1))  # (sets, rules, j)
    rule_lik = (e_rule * c_set[:, None, :]).sum(axis=2)
    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) - np.log(N_RULES) + pt.log(rule_lik)

    # Ranges: Gaussian-kernel interpolation of the tabulated logs in logit(r).
    kernel = pt.exp(-0.5 * ((r_logit - GRID) / GRID_STEP) ** 2)
    kw = kernel / kernel.sum()
    e_range = pt.exp(pt.tensordot(kw, range_log_e, axes=[[0], [0]]))  # (sets, S)
    num_range = pt.exp(pt.tensordot(kw, range_log_cell, axes=[[0], [0]]))  # (cells, S)
    range_ev = (e_range * w_sub).sum(axis=1)
    log_ranges = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(5050.0) + pt.log(range_ev)
    range_share = (num_range * w_sub[cell_set]).sum(axis=1) / range_ev[cell_set]

    log_joint = pt.concatenate([log_rules, log_ranges[:, None]], axis=1)
    log_norm = pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1)
    rule_post = pt.exp(log_rules - log_norm[:, None])
    range_post = pt.exp(log_ranges - log_norm)

    rule_endorse = pt.exp(log_r * RULE_DMIN)  # (rules, numbers)
    set_endorse = pt.dot(rule_post, rule_endorse)  # (sets, numbers)
    rule_part = set_endorse.flatten()[cell_flat]
    p_cell = rule_part + range_post[cell_set] * range_share
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(p_cell, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)[row_cell])
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def _distance_counts(example_idx, example_mask):
    """Number of each rule's members at distance d (0..MAX_D) from each example."""
    out = np.zeros(example_idx.shape + (N_RULES, MAX_D + 1))
    for d in range(MAX_D + 1):
        near = (ABS_DIFF == d).astype("float64")  # (numbers, numbers)
        out[..., d] = (near[example_idx] @ RULE_MEMBERSHIP.T) * example_mask[..., None]
    return out


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    S = len(unique)
    example_idx = np.zeros((S, MAX_N), dtype="int64")
    example_mask = np.zeros((S, MAX_N))
    set_n_idx = np.zeros(S, dtype="int64")
    for i, s in enumerate(unique):
        n = len(s)
        set_n_idx[i] = n - 1
        example_idx[i, :n] = np.array(s) - 1
        example_mask[i, :n] = 1.0
    keys = [(index[s], int(r["target"])) for s, r in zip(sets, rows)]
    cells = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    cell_index = {c: j for j, c in enumerate(cells)}
    cell_set = np.array([i for i, _ in cells], dtype="int64")
    cell_target = np.array([t - 1 for _, t in cells], dtype="int64")
    log_e, log_cell = range_tables(example_idx, example_mask, cell_set, cell_target)
    return {
        "example_idx": example_idx,
        "example_mask": example_mask,
        "set_n_idx": set_n_idx,
        "range_log_e": log_e,
        "range_log_cell": log_cell,
        "cell_set": cell_set,
        "cell_n_idx": set_n_idx[cell_set],
        "ex_rule_dcount": _distance_counts(example_idx, example_mask),
        "cell_flat": cell_set * 100 + cell_target,
        "cell_target": cell_target,
        "row_cell": np.array([cell_index[c] for c in keys], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

_N = np.arange(1, MAX_N + 1, dtype="float64")[:, None]
_J = np.arange(MAX_N + 1, dtype="float64")[None, :]
_VALID = _J <= _N
_N_MINUS_J = np.maximum(_N - _J, 0.0)


def _betaln(a, b):
    return pt.gammaln(a) + pt.gammaln(b) - pt.gammaln(a + b)


def _elementary(weights, lib=pt):
    """Elementary symmetric polynomials e_0..e_4 over the last axis (4 examples)."""
    ones = lib.ones_like(weights[..., 0])
    e = [ones] + [ones * 0.0] * MAX_N
    for i in range(MAX_N):
        w = weights[..., i]
        e = [e[0]] + [e[j] + w * e[j - 1] for j in range(1, MAX_N + 1)]
    return lib.stack(e, axis=-1)


def range_tables(example_idx, example_mask, cell_set, cell_target):
    """Per logit(r) grid point: log sum over ranges of prod_{i in S} 100 s_i(h)
    per set and subset S, and the same weighted by each cell target's
    similarity to the range (cells, S)."""
    lo = np.array([m for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)], dtype="float64")[:, None]
    hi = np.array([n for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)], dtype="float64")[:, None]
    size = hi - lo + 1
    x = NUMBERS[None, :].astype("float64")
    inside = (x >= lo) & (x <= hi)
    dmin = np.maximum(0.0, np.maximum(lo - x, x - hi))
    S, C = example_idx.shape[0], len(cell_set)
    K = len(SUBSETS)
    log_set = np.zeros((len(GRID), S, K))
    log_cell = np.zeros((len(GRID), C, K))
    cells_of = [np.where(cell_set == s)[0] for s in range(S)]
    for g, logit_r in enumerate(GRID):
        r = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-logit_r))
        geo = r / (1 - r)
        summed = np.where(
            inside,
            1 + geo * (2 - r ** np.where(inside, x - lo, 0) - r ** np.where(inside, hi - x, 0)),
            r**dmin * (1 - r**size) / (1 - r),
        )
        w100 = 100.0 * summed / size  # (ranges, numbers)
        endorse = r**dmin  # (ranges, numbers)
        for s in range(S):
            wts = w100[:, example_idx[s]] * example_mask[s][None, :]  # (ranges, 4)
            prods = np.prod(np.where(SUBSETS[None, :, :], wts[:, None, :], 1.0), axis=2)  # (ranges, 16)
            log_set[g, s] = np.log(np.maximum(prods.sum(axis=0), 1e-300))
            cs = cells_of[s]
            if len(cs):
                num = endorse[:, cell_target[cs]].T @ prods  # (k, 16)
                log_cell[g, cs] = np.log(np.maximum(num, 1e-300))
    return log_set, log_cell


with pm.Model() as model:
    example_idx = pm.Data("example_idx", np.zeros((1, MAX_N), dtype="int64"))  # x - 1
    example_mask = pm.Data("example_mask", np.zeros((1, MAX_N)))
    set_n_idx = pm.Data("set_n_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    range_log_e = pm.Data("range_log_e", np.zeros((len(GRID), 1, len(SUBSETS))))  # (grid, sets, S)
    range_log_cell = pm.Data("range_log_cell", np.zeros((len(GRID), 1, len(SUBSETS))))  # (grid, cells, S)
    cell_set = pm.Data("cell_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cell_target = pm.Data("cell_target", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # target - 1
    cell_n_idx = pm.Data("cell_n_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # (cells,): n - 1
    ex_rule_dcount = pm.Data("ex_rule_dcount", np.zeros((1, MAX_N, N_RULES, MAX_D + 1)))  # members at distance d
    cell_flat = pm.Data("cell_flat", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set * 100 + target - 1
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    alpha_logit = pm.Normal("alpha_logit", mu=2.2, sigma=1.5)
    alpha = pm.Deterministic("alpha", pm.math.sigmoid(alpha_logit))
    log_kappa = pm.Normal("log_kappa", mu=np.log(10.0), sigma=1.0)
    kappa = pm.Deterministic("kappa", pt.exp(log_kappa))
    u, v = alpha * kappa, (1 - alpha) * kappa

    # Number-line similarity gradient s(x, y) = r^|x - y|.
    r_logit = pm.TruncatedNormal("r_logit", mu=-4.0, sigma=1.0, lower=GRID[0], upper=GRID[-1])
    r = pm.Deterministic("r", pm.math.sigmoid(r_logit))
    log_r = pt.log(r)

    c_table = pt.where(_VALID, pt.exp(_betaln(u + _J, v + _N_MINUS_J) - _betaln(u, v)), 0.0)
    c_set = c_table[set_n_idx]  # (sets, j)

    # Stray distribution: uniform mixed with a random member of a random rule.
    mix_logit = pm.Normal("mix_logit", mu=0.0, sigma=1.5)
    mix = pm.Deterministic("mix", pm.math.sigmoid(mix_logit))
    rho = 1.0 / ((1 - mix) + mix * 100.0 * STRAY_RULE_GEN)  # (numbers,): 1 / (100 q)
    rho_ex = rho[example_idx]  # (sets, 4); masked examples have zero weight anyway
    rho_sub = pt.prod(pt.where(SUBSETS[None, :, :], rho_ex[:, None, :], 1.0), axis=2)  # (sets, 16)
    w_sub = c_set[:, SUBSET_SIZE] * rho_sub  # (sets, 16)

    # Rules: mean similarity of each example to the rule's stored members.
    r_pow = pt.exp(log_r * np.arange(MAX_D + 1))
    w_rule = 100.0 * pt.dot(ex_rule_dcount, r_pow) / RULE_SIZE  # (sets, 4, rules), masked via counts
    e_rule = _elementary((w_rule * rho_ex[:, :, None]).dimshuffle(0, 2, 1))  # (sets, rules, j)
    rule_lik = (e_rule * c_set[:, None, :]).sum(axis=2)
    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) - np.log(N_RULES) + pt.log(rule_lik)

    # Ranges: Gaussian-kernel interpolation of the tabulated logs in logit(r).
    kernel = pt.exp(-0.5 * ((r_logit - GRID) / GRID_STEP) ** 2)
    kw = kernel / kernel.sum()
    e_range = pt.exp(pt.tensordot(kw, range_log_e, axes=[[0], [0]]))  # (sets, S)
    num_range = pt.exp(pt.tensordot(kw, range_log_cell, axes=[[0], [0]]))  # (cells, S)
    range_ev = (e_range * w_sub).sum(axis=1)
    log_ranges = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(5050.0) + pt.log(range_ev)
    range_share = (num_range * w_sub[cell_set]).sum(axis=1) / range_ev[cell_set]

    log_joint = pt.concatenate([log_rules, log_ranges[:, None]], axis=1)
    log_norm = pt.logsumexp(log_joint, axis=1)
    rule_post = pt.exp(log_rules - log_norm[:, None])
    range_post = pt.exp(log_ranges - log_norm)

    rule_endorse = pt.exp(log_r * RULE_DMIN)  # (rules, numbers)
    set_endorse = pt.dot(rule_post, rule_endorse)  # (sets, numbers)
    rule_part = set_endorse.flatten()[cell_flat]
    p_cell = rule_part + range_post[cell_set] * range_share
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(p_cell, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)[row_cell])
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def _distance_counts(example_idx, example_mask):
    """Number of each rule's members at distance d (0..MAX_D) from each example."""
    out = np.zeros(example_idx.shape + (N_RULES, MAX_D + 1))
    for d in range(MAX_D + 1):
        near = (ABS_DIFF == d).astype("float64")  # (numbers, numbers)
        out[..., d] = (near[example_idx] @ RULE_MEMBERSHIP.T) * example_mask[..., None]
    return out


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    S = len(unique)
    example_idx = np.zeros((S, MAX_N), dtype="int64")
    example_mask = np.zeros((S, MAX_N))
    set_n_idx = np.zeros(S, dtype="int64")
    for i, s in enumerate(unique):
        n = len(s)
        set_n_idx[i] = n - 1
        example_idx[i, :n] = np.array(s) - 1
        example_mask[i, :n] = 1.0
    keys = [(index[s], int(r["target"])) for s, r in zip(sets, rows)]
    cells = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    cell_index = {c: j for j, c in enumerate(cells)}
    cell_set = np.array([i for i, _ in cells], dtype="int64")
    cell_target = np.array([t - 1 for _, t in cells], dtype="int64")
    log_e, log_cell = range_tables(example_idx, example_mask, cell_set, cell_target)
    return {
        "example_idx": example_idx,
        "example_mask": example_mask,
        "set_n_idx": set_n_idx,
        "range_log_e": log_e,
        "range_log_cell": log_cell,
        "cell_set": cell_set,
        "cell_n_idx": set_n_idx[cell_set],
        "ex_rule_dcount": _distance_counts(example_idx, example_mask),
        "cell_flat": cell_set * 100 + cell_target,
        "cell_target": cell_target,
        "row_cell": np.array([cell_index[c] for c in keys], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

"""Two-source program whose glitches are familiar numbers.

Refinement of two_source_program_concepts. People think the hidden program may
run two sources at once: a main concept c1 (one of 45 rules, prior lambda_0/45
each, or an interval of 1-100, prior (1-lambda_0)/100^2 each), from which each
example is a size-principle draw with uncertain reliability
a ~ Beta(alpha*kappa, (1-alpha)*kappa), and one secondary source per set that
produced the remaining (stray) examples: a second familiar rule c2 that is
generalised from (prior mix/45 each), or glitches (prior 1-mix) that license
no generalisation. The one change, taken from rule_count_familiar_strays, is
what a glitch looks like: not uniform over 1-100, but with inferred probability
g a "familiar" number, drawn in proportion to how many of the 45 rules contain
it (q(x) = (1-g)/100 + g * #rules(x) / sum_y #rules(y)). So richly connected
off-pattern numbers (12, 24, 36, 60, 100) are cheap to write off as glitches
without endorsing any rule they fit, while unremarkable off-pattern numbers
that fit a small rule are better explained as that second rule's output.

For a set with examples X (n of them), concept pair (c1, src) and a split of
the examples into genuine G (|G| = j) and strays X\\G:
  p(X, G | c1, src) = B(u+j, v+n-j)/B(u,v) * prod_G 1[x in c1]/|c1| * prod_{X\\G} q_src(x).
The second-rule part is summed in prepare_observed into tables E[set, class, j]
and Y[cell, class, j]; the glitch part keeps the subset G axis (16 subsets),
so prod_{X\\G} 100 q(x) is applied in the model.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
MAX_N = 4


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return rules


RULES = list(rule_concepts().values())
N_RULES = len(RULES)
RULE_MEM = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES], dtype="float64")  # (rules, 100)
RULE_SIZE = RULE_MEM.sum(axis=1)
INT_LO = np.array([m for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)])
INT_HI = np.array([n for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)])
INT_SIZE = (INT_HI - INT_LO + 1).astype("float64")
INT_MEM = ((NUMBERS[None, :] >= INT_LO[:, None]) & (NUMBERS[None, :] <= INT_HI[:, None])).astype("float64")

_N = np.arange(1, MAX_N + 1, dtype="float64")[:, None]
_J = np.arange(MAX_N + 1, dtype="float64")[None, :]
_VALID = _J <= _N
_N_MINUS_J = np.maximum(_N - _J, 0.0)
N_SUB = 2**MAX_N
SUBSETS = np.array([[(m >> i) & 1 for i in range(MAX_N)] for m in range(N_SUB)], dtype=bool)  # (16, 4)
SUBSET_SIZE = SUBSETS.sum(axis=1)
RULE_COUNT_FAMILIARITY = RULE_MEM.sum(axis=0) / RULE_MEM.sum()  # (100,)


def _betaln(a, b):
    return pt.gammaln(a) + pt.gammaln(b) - pt.gammaln(a + b)


with pm.Model() as model:
    ev_rule = pm.Data("ev_rule", np.zeros((1, 2, MAX_N + 1)))  # (sets, class, j): second-rule source
    yes_rule = pm.Data("yes_rule", np.zeros((1, 2, MAX_N + 1)))  # (cells, class, j)
    ev_glitch = pm.Data("ev_glitch", np.zeros((1, 2, N_SUB)))  # (sets, class, subset G): glitch source
    yes_glitch = pm.Data("yes_glitch", np.zeros((1, 2, N_SUB)))  # (cells, class, subset G)
    example_idx = pm.Data("example_idx", np.zeros((1, MAX_N), dtype="int64"))  # x - 1, shown order
    example_mask = pm.Data("example_mask", np.zeros((1, MAX_N)))
    set_n_idx = pm.Data("set_n_idx", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    cell_set = pm.Data("cell_set", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    alpha_logit = pm.Normal("alpha_logit", mu=2.2, sigma=1.5)
    alpha = pm.Deterministic("alpha", pm.math.sigmoid(alpha_logit))
    log_kappa = pm.Normal("log_kappa", mu=np.log(10.0), sigma=1.0)
    kappa = pm.Deterministic("kappa", pt.exp(log_kappa))
    u, v = alpha * kappa, (1 - alpha) * kappa
    mix_logit = pm.Normal("mix_logit", mu=0.0, sigma=1.5)
    mix = pm.Deterministic("mix", pm.math.sigmoid(mix_logit))  # prior that the second source is a rule
    # Glitches: uniform, or with probability g a familiar number (rule-count familiarity).
    g_logit = pm.Normal("g_logit", mu=0.0, sigma=1.5)
    g = pm.Deterministic("g", pm.math.sigmoid(g_logit))
    q_rel = (1 - g) + g * 100.0 * RULE_COUNT_FAMILIARITY  # (100,): 100 q(x)
    q_ex = pt.where(example_mask > 0, q_rel[example_idx], 1.0)  # (sets, 4)
    stray_fac = pt.prod(pt.where(SUBSETS[None, :, :], 1.0, q_ex[:, None, :]), axis=2)  # (sets, 16)

    c_table = pt.where(_VALID, pt.exp(_betaln(u + _J, v + _N_MINUS_J) - _betaln(u, v)), 0.0)
    c_set = c_table[set_n_idx]  # (sets, j)
    w_class = pt.stack([lambda_0, 1 - lambda_0])
    w_rule = mix * w_class[None, :, None] * c_set[:, None, :]  # (sets, class, j)
    w_glitch = (1 - mix) * w_class[None, :, None] * (c_set[:, SUBSET_SIZE] * stray_fac)[:, None, :]  # (sets, class, 16)
    evidence = (w_rule * ev_rule).sum(axis=(1, 2)) + (w_glitch * ev_glitch).sum(axis=(1, 2))
    yes_mass = (w_rule[cell_set] * yes_rule).sum(axis=(1, 2)) + (w_glitch[cell_set] * yes_glitch).sum(axis=(1, 2))
    p_cell = yes_mass / evidence[cell_set]
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip(p_cell, 1e-9, 1 - 1e-9)[row_cell])
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def _set_tables(ex):
    """Second-rule tables (class, j) and glitch tables (class, subset) for one set, with yes-mass per target."""
    n = len(ex)
    n_sub = 2**n
    sub_in = np.array([[(m >> i) & 1 for i in range(n)] for m in range(n_sub)], dtype=bool)  # (G, n)
    j_of = sub_in.sum(axis=1)
    full = n_sub - 1
    onehot_j = np.zeros((n_sub, MAX_N + 1))
    onehot_j[np.arange(n_sub), j_of] = 1.0

    def genuine_w(mem, size, prior):  # G must lie in c1: weight prior * size^-j
        ex_in = mem[:, ex - 1] > 0  # (concepts, n)
        ok = ~(sub_in[None, :, :] & ~ex_in[:, None, :]).any(axis=2)  # (concepts, G)
        return ok * size[:, None] ** -j_of[None, :] * prior

    w1 = [genuine_w(RULE_MEM, RULE_SIZE, 1.0 / N_RULES), genuine_w(INT_MEM, INT_SIZE, 1.0 / 100**2)]
    w1_tot = [w.sum(axis=0) for w in w1]  # (G,)
    w1_out = [RULE_MEM_NOT.T @ w1[0], INT_MEM_NOT.T @ w1[1]]  # (100, G): c1 lacks target
    # Second-rule source: strays X\\G must lie in c2.
    ex_in2 = RULE_MEM[:, ex - 1] > 0
    ok2 = ~((~sub_in)[None, :, :] & ~ex_in2[:, None, :]).any(axis=2)
    w2 = ok2 * RULE_SIZE[:, None] ** -(n - j_of)[None, :] / N_RULES  # (rules, G)
    w2_tot = w2.sum(axis=0)
    w2_out = RULE_MEM_NOT.T @ w2  # (100, G): c2 lacks target
    w2_out[:, full] = w2_tot[full]  # no strays: the second rule produced nothing, no generalisation
    w_unif = 0.01 ** (n - j_of)

    ev_r = np.zeros((2, MAX_N + 1))
    yes_r = np.zeros((100, 2, MAX_N + 1))
    ev_g = np.zeros((2, N_SUB))  # subsets beyond 2^n stay zero
    yes_g = np.zeros((100, 2, N_SUB))
    for k in range(2):
        ev_r[k] = (w1_tot[k] * w2_tot) @ onehot_j
        yes_r[:, k] = (w1_tot[k] * w2_tot - w1_out[k] * w2_out) @ onehot_j
        ev_g[k, :n_sub] = w1_tot[k] * w_unif
        yes_g[:, k, :n_sub] = (w1_tot[k] - w1_out[k]) * w_unif
    scale = max(ev_r.max(), ev_g.max())
    return ev_r / scale, yes_r / scale, ev_g / scale, yes_g / scale


RULE_MEM_NOT = 1.0 - RULE_MEM
INT_MEM_NOT = 1.0 - INT_MEM


def prepare_observed(rows):
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    tables = [_set_tables(np.array(s)) for s in unique]
    keys = [(index[s], int(r["target"])) for s, r in zip(sets, rows)]
    cells = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    cell_index = {c: k for k, c in enumerate(cells)}
    S = len(unique)
    example_idx = np.zeros((S, MAX_N), dtype="int64")
    example_mask = np.zeros((S, MAX_N))
    for i, s in enumerate(unique):
        example_idx[i, : len(s)] = np.array(s) - 1
        example_mask[i, : len(s)] = 1.0
    return {
        "ev_rule": np.stack([t[0] for t in tables]),
        "yes_rule": np.stack([tables[i][1][t - 1] for i, t in cells]),
        "ev_glitch": np.stack([t[2] for t in tables]),
        "yes_glitch": np.stack([tables[i][3][t - 1] for i, t in cells]),
        "example_idx": example_idx,
        "example_mask": example_mask,
        "set_n_idx": np.array([len(s) - 1 for s in unique], dtype="int64"),

content.text:
I submitted `two_source_range_limited_rules` in candidate_5, and it passes the admission check. It refines `two_source_familiar_glitches` with one change taken from the incumbent: the main concept can now also be a rule applied only within a magnitude range ("odd numbers from 9 to 33"), with an inferred share of the rule prior. The two-source part is unchanged: an off-pattern example is either a second rule people generalise from, or a glitch that is sometimes a familiar number.

**Fit (MAP on the full data):**
- Log-likelihood is −3321.13, against −3322.25 for its parent and about −3320.8 for the incumbent.
- Both mechanisms stay active: the range-limited rules take 10% of the rule prior, and the second-rule source gets 4%.
- Its predictions differ from the incumbent's by RMSE 0.0075 on the observed stimuli. The admission gate measures this on a different stimulus pool, and earlier runs showed the pool figure to be about half the data figure. That would put it near 0.004, against a threshold of about 0.002, so I expect it to pass, but novelty is the part not yet checked.
- The smoke fit took 12 s and gave a log-likelihood of −3323.1.

**On the critique:** this model does not close the span-contrast gap, and I didn't find anything that does.
- The gap is on the narrow side. For rule sets whose examples span 40 or less, people say yes to non-members inside the span 52% of the time, against about 41% predicted. Wide spans fit (22% vs 21%).
- Every live model I fitted (six of them) predicts 41–43% there. The gap comes mostly from a few 5-response cells, mainly "31,3,1,15" → 2, 4, 16 (93% yes vs 53% predicted).
- A prior favouring narrow magnitude ranges is the obvious fix, and it failed again. An exponential width prior drifted back to uniform with no gain, and a Tenenbaum-style (Erlang) width prior lost 3.7 nats.

I saved these findings to the memory notes so later rounds don't retry the width priors.

Files are in `iter_1/candidate_5/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
